newsitem.title: BRAZIL: FORECAST - Telebras '97 net still seen strong.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Telebras '97 net still seen strong.

text.p: Higher charges, rising use and a surge in new cellular lines will ensure hefty year-end profits at Brazilian giant Telebras, despite mildly disappointing first quarter results, analysts said.
"I expected a little more in the first quarter but the results were not scary," said Marcelo Mollica of Banco Icatu. "The outlook is still very good."

Bank analysts surveyed by Reuters said they are leaving mostly unchanged their 1997 earnings forecasts for Latin America's largest telecommunications firm, following the release of first-quarter figures.

They forecast that Telebras will post consolidated year-end net profit of between $3.3 billion and $3.5 billion, up sharply from last year's $2.54 billion net profit. Projections for 1998 range from $3.6 billion to $4.2 billion.
"The main factor is revenues as a result of the rise in tariffs," said Veri Rossi, a telecoms analyst at ING Barings in Brazil.

The Brazilian government this week instituted the third and final round of rate adjustments, including a 270-percent hike in the residential subscription rate and 59-percent rises in non-residential and trunk rates.

Slated to be broken up and privatized starting in early 1998, the state giant on May 14 posted a first-quarter consolidated net profit of 691 million reais ($650 million), including a 103 million-real non-recurring expense linked to long-distance unit Embratel's telex plant.
Many analysts had projected Telebras results of between 700 million reais and 800 million reais, and had not counted on the Embratel expense.
"Without that provision, the result was well within market expectations," said Sergio Missima of Banco Fator.
Analysts also said line growth, especially cellular terminals, was slower than they hoped but added that installation of new lines is usually slow in the first three months of the year.

They projected an explosion in new cellular lines later this year as Telebras' subsidiaries prepare for stiff competition from operators on a newly privatized B Band. Licenses to operate on the B Band frequency are expected to be awarded starting next month.
"These bids could fuel higher valuation for Telebras and its subsidiaries," Caspian Securities said in a report.
Another reason for optimism regarding Telebras are the bright prospects for its privatization, analysts said.
Those prospects received an added boost this week when a panel of the Brazilian Congress' lower house approved a bill regulating the country's telecoms sector and outlining Telebras' privatization.
The General Telecommunications Law still must be approved by the full Chamber of Deputies, where officials hope for a vote in June, then pass in the Senate.
Officials expect its final approval in July, but analysts said it may take longer.
